_note: Rotates one story per day. Read each passage in the NLT. Add more stories in the same shape.

stories.prayer: God, give me the strength to do the right thing when nobody's watching.
stories.q1: Joseph was a slave with nothing to lose by giving in. Why do you think he still said no?
stories.q2: He didn't argue with the temptation. He ran. What's one thing you should run from instead of negotiating with?
stories.q3: Joseph did the right thing and still ended up in prison. How do you keep going when doing right costs you?
stories.action: Name one temptation you usually negotiate with, and set up one barrier against it today.

stories.prayer: Lord, help me face today's giants with faith instead of fear.
stories.q1: David's confidence came from times God had already helped him. What has God already brought you through?
stories.q2: Saul's armor didn't fit David, so he used what he knew. What tools has God already put in your hands?
stories.q3: Everyone else saw how big Goliath was. David saw how big God was. What are you staring at too hard right now?
stories.action: Do the one task you've been avoiding because it feels too big. Start it before noon.

stories.prayer: God, make me consistent, the same man in private as in public.
stories.q1: Daniel's enemies couldn't find anything wrong with him except his faith. What would people find if they looked at your habits?
stories.q2: Daniel kept praying three times a day even when it became illegal. What daily habit with God would you protect at any cost?
stories.q3: Daniel was excellent at his job. How does doing your schoolwork well connect to your faith?
stories.action: Pick a set time to pray tomorrow and put it in your calendar.

stories.prayer: Father, thank you for running toward me when I come back.
stories.q1: The younger son 'came to his senses.' What usually makes you realize you've drifted?
stories.q2: The older brother never left, but he was still far from his father's heart. Where could you be doing the right things with the wrong heart?
stories.q3: What does the father running to his son tell you about how God sees your mistakes?
stories.action: Reach out to one person you've drifted from: a text, a call, or an apology.

stories.prayer: Lord, help me finish what I start, and keep building even when people mock it.
stories.q1: Sanballat mocked the builders. How do you handle people who doubt what you're building?
stories.q2: They worked with one hand and held a weapon in the other. What do you need to guard while you build?
stories.q3: The wall went up because everyone took their section. What's your section right now?
stories.action: Spend 25 minutes building something real (Jarvis, MATLAB, or your trade log) instead of scrolling.

stories.prayer: Jesus, teach me to lead by serving.
stories.q1: Jesus knew he had all authority, and he picked up a towel. What does that say about real strength?
stories.q2: Peter tried to refuse. Why is it sometimes harder to receive help than to give it?
stories.q3: Who around you needs a 'foot washing,' a humble act nobody would expect from you?
stories.action: Do one unasked-for chore or favor for someone at home today, and don't mention it.

stories.prayer: Lord, keep my eyes on you, not on the waves.
stories.q1: Peter was the only one who got out of the boat. What's a 'get out of the boat' step you've been holding back on?
stories.q2: He started sinking when he looked at the wind. What 'wind' pulls your focus off God?
stories.q3: Jesus caught him immediately. How does that change how you think about failing while trying?
stories.action: Take one step on something that scares you a little: ask a question in class, message your uncle, or similar.

stories.prayer: God, open my eyes to the people I usually walk past.
stories.q1: The priest and the Levite had reasons to keep walking. What reasons do you use to avoid getting involved?
stories.q2: The hero was someone the listeners looked down on. Who might you be underestimating?
stories.q3: The Samaritan paid with time and money. What would it cost you to really help someone this week?
stories.action: Notice one person who's struggling today and do something concrete for them.

stories.prayer: Lord, I'll trust you even when I feel like I don't have enough.
stories.q1: God cut Gideon's army from 32,000 to 300. Why would God make the odds worse on purpose?
stories.q2: Gideon needed reassurance more than once, and God gave it. How honest are you with God about your doubts?
stories.q3: Where in your life are you waiting to have 'enough' before you start?
stories.action: Start something today with what you have now, instead of waiting until you're ready.

stories.story: Jesus is tempted in the wilderness
stories.prayer: Jesus, help me answer temptation the way you did, with truth.
stories.q1: The devil came when Jesus was hungry and tired. When are you most vulnerable? Mornings, late nights?
stories.q2: Jesus answered every temptation with Scripture. What verse could you keep ready for your weak moments?
stories.q3: Each temptation offered a shortcut. What shortcut are you tempted by right now?
stories.action: Write one verse on a sticky note and put it where you usually grab your phone.

stories.prayer: God, help me obey you even when it looks strange to everyone around me.
stories.q1: Noah built for years before a drop of rain fell. What are you building now that won't pay off for a while?
stories.q2: Everyone around Noah went the other way. How do you hold your ground when your friends don't?
stories.q3: Noah did everything exactly as God commanded. Where are you doing 90% of what you know is right?
stories.action: Pick one thing you've been half-doing and finish it completely today.

stories.prayer: Lord, when I feel unqualified, remind me that you go with me.
stories.q1: Moses gave God excuse after excuse. What's your favorite excuse for not stepping up?
stories.q2: God's answer wasn't 'you're good enough' but 'I will be with you.' How does that change the pressure on you?
stories.q3: Moses was doing an ordinary job when God showed up. How might God use your ordinary days?
stories.action: Do one thing today you've been telling yourself you're not ready for.

stories.story: Joshua and the walls of Jericho
stories.prayer: God, give me patience to follow your plan even when it doesn't make sense yet.
stories.q1: Marching in circles for seven days looked pointless. Where do you need to keep going without seeing results?
stories.q2: The plan only worked because the whole team followed it. Who are you letting down when you skip your part?
stories.q3: The victory came from God, not their strength. What are you trying to win on your own?
stories.action: Show up fully for one boring, repeated task today without complaining.

stories.prayer: Father, make me loyal to the people you've put in my life.
stories.q1: Ruth had every reason to leave. Why do you think she stayed?
stories.q2: Loyalty cost Ruth her comfort. What has being loyal cost you, and was it worth it?
stories.q3: Who in your life needs you to stick around right now?
stories.action: Reach out to one family member or friend today just to check on them.

stories.prayer: Lord, give me the courage to stand for you when I'm outnumbered.
stories.q1: Elijah asked the people how long they'd waver between two opinions. Where are you wavering?
stories.q2: Elijah made it harder on himself by soaking the altar. Why do you think he did that?
stories.q3: He stood alone against 450. What would standing for your faith look like at school this week?
stories.action: Make one decision today that you've been sitting on the fence about.

stories.prayer: God, help me use whatever position you've given me to do what's right.
stories.q1: Mordecai said maybe Esther was put there 'for just such a time as this.' Where might God have put you on purpose?
stories.q2: Esther prepared before acting. How do you prepare for hard conversations?
stories.q3: She risked her life for her people. What's one risk worth taking for someone else?
stories.action: Use one advantage you have today to help someone who doesn't have it.

stories.prayer: Father, when I'm running from what you've asked, turn me around.
stories.q1: Jonah didn't just say no, he ran the opposite direction. What are you running from?
stories.q2: His running put other people in danger too. Who gets hurt when you avoid what you should do?
stories.q3: God gave Jonah a second chance. What second chance do you need to take?
stories.action: Do the thing you've been avoiding the longest, or at least the first step of it.

stories.prayer: Lord, make my faith steady even if things don't go my way.
stories.q1: They said God could save them, but even if he didn't, they wouldn't bow. What does 'even if he doesn't' faith look like for you?
stories.q2: They didn't have to make a speech; they just didn't bow. Where does quiet obedience matter most for you?
stories.q3: Someone was with them in the fire. When have you felt God with you in a hard spot?
stories.action: Refuse one small compromise today that you'd normally go along with.

stories.prayer: Jesus, when my life feels like a storm, help me trust that you're in the boat.
stories.q1: The disciples asked if Jesus even cared. When have you felt like God was asleep?
stories.q2: Jesus asked why they were afraid. What's the biggest fear you're carrying right now?
stories.q3: The storm obeyed him. What would change if you really believed he's in control?
stories.action: Write down one worry and pray over it, then leave it there and get to work.

stories.prayer: Lord, show me where I need to change, and give me the guts to actually do it.
stories.q1: Zacchaeus went out of his way just to see Jesus. How far are you willing to go to grow?
stories.q2: Jesus chose to eat with the guy everyone hated. Who do you overlook?
stories.q3: Zacchaeus didn't just feel sorry; he paid people back. What does real change look like for you?
stories.action: Make one thing right today: return, repay, or apologize for something.

stories.prayer: Jesus, thank you that my failures aren't the end of my story.
stories.q1: Peter denied Jesus three times, and Jesus asked him three times if he loved him. Why do you think he did it that way?
stories.q2: Jesus didn't lecture Peter; he gave him a job. What does that say about how God handles failure?
stories.q3: What past failure are you still carrying that God has already dealt with?
stories.action: Let go of one past mistake today, and do one useful thing for someone else instead.

stories.prayer: God, teach me to praise you even when things are going wrong.
stories.q1: Beaten and chained, they sang at midnight. What's your 'midnight' right now?
stories.q2: When the doors opened they stayed, and it saved the jailer's life. When does staying put matter?
stories.q3: Their worship affected everyone in the prison. Who is watching how you handle hard times?
stories.action: When something goes wrong today, respond with gratitude first before you complain.
